title: Operation kind (platform-vocabulary classifier over closure-rule patterns)
description: Regime: stable-aperiodic-articulation-cell (platform-vocabulary classifier). Derivation from the four-regime grammar in CLAUDE.md: operation-kind is meta — it CLASSIFIES closure-rule patterns rather than itself being a closure-rule pattern. The seven kinds it enumerates (observation, guard, accounting, query, mutation, analysis, learning) describe operations whose own regimes vary: a query is finite-settlement-algebra, a learning operation may span aperiodic ingestion + transfinite predication + Scott-continuous positing + finite settlement. Each individual operation-kind RECORD is a finite description of one pattern, but the classifier as platform vocabulary sits at the stable-aperiodic-articulation-cell level (where AOP-internal vocabulary lives). Per lab/.../operation-kinds/operation-kinds.md (a pre-stabilization note that nonetheless got the seven kinds right): 'The platform's operations decompose into a small number of structural kinds, each characterized by what it reads, what it writes, and what closure rule pattern produces it.' Particular platform operations may compose multiple kinds (a dispatch decision is guard followed by mutation; a runbook execution sequences queries, mutations, and observations).
